How it works

From booking to return, step by step

No shop to find, no queue, no haggling. This is what happens after you book, every rental day.

  1. Book

    You book online

    Choose your ride, rental dates and where you stay. It takes two minutes and you pay nothing yet.

  2. Delivery

    Your ride comes to you

    You pick a delivery time slot. Our staff hand you the key, with two helmets and two raincoats (for motorbikes), show you how it works and take a photo of your ID. You sign the rental agreement and pay. No deposit.

  3. Explore

    You ride freely

    Rice fields, river roads, temples, a slow lunch. No petrol stops, no noise. Need help? Just message the shop.

  4. Return

    Our staff collect the ride

    At where you stay, at the time agreed on delivery. You can still extend your rental; late returns may incur an extra fee.

Choose your ride, all electric

Electric motorbike

VinFast Evo Lite

Twist and go. No gears, no clutch, no noise. It seats two, so one bike is enough for a couple.

  • Top speed 49 km/h, no licence needed
  • About 60 km per charge, and a day of exploring is usually 30–60 km
  • Two helmets, two raincoats and a phone holder
  • Under 100 kg, easy to handle even for first-timers

Good for: foreign travellers, and riders over 16 without a driving licence.

E-bike

Phoenix Assist

Good for: riders who enjoy cycling and want to go far without much effort.

Places

Every place worth visiting is just a short ride away

Road distances from the boat pier in the middle of Tam Coc. One charge covers them all, with plenty to spare.

  1. 3km

    Bich Dong Pagoda Chùa Bích Động

    Three small pagodas perched on a cliff. The road there winds between lotus ponds and limestone peaks — the most beautiful short ride in the area.

    E-bike or motorbike
  2. 5km

    Mua Cave viewpoint Hang Múa

    Nearly 500 steps lead to a panoramic view over the Tam Coc valley. Best early in the morning or at sunset.

    E-bike or motorbike
  3. 8km

    Thung Nham bird valley Vườn chim Thung Nham

    A quiet valley where thousands of storks and herons come home to roost in the late afternoon.

    E-bike or motorbike
  4. 10km

    Trang An boat tours Tràng An

    The UNESCO-listed boat route through caves and past temples. Go early, before the big tour groups arrive.

    E-bike or motorbike
  5. 16km

    Hoa Lu ancient capital Cố đô Hoa Lư

    Vietnam's capital a thousand years ago. Two temples to its founding kings, set among majestic mountains.

    Better by motorbike
  6. 25km

    Bai Dinh Pagoda Chùa Bái Đính

    One of the largest Buddhist temple complexes in Southeast Asia. Combine it with Trang An for a full day.

    Better by motorbike

And the Tam Coc boat trip? The pier is right in the middle of the village — you can walk there.

Answers

What guests often ask

Do I need a driving licence?

Not for the Evo Lite or the e-bike. The Evo Lite is limited to 49 km/h — in Vietnam, electric motorbikes under this limit may be ridden from age 16 without a licence.

Note: check whether your travel insurance covers riding.

Do I have to leave my passport?

No, and no deposit either. Our staff just take a photo of your passport (or licence) for the paperwork, then you sign a short rental agreement. The original passport stays in your pocket.

I have never ridden a motorbike. Should I worry?

The Evo Lite is very easy to ride: fully automatic, under 100 kg and a top speed of only 49 km/h. The delivery staff will show you on the spot.

Still unsure? Choose the e-bike. If you can ride a bicycle, you can ride it right away.

What if the battery runs out?

Very unlikely. The motorbike runs about 80 km per charge, while a day of exploring is usually only 30–60 km.

Running low anyway? Message the shop and they will send you the address of the nearest swap station — open day and night.

What if the bike breaks down or I get a flat tyre?

Message your location to the shop and they will help you. The bikes are new, so problems are rare.

Can I cancel or change my booking?

Absolutely, and for free, since you have not paid anything. Just message the shop as early as possible, ideally the evening before.
